name: Joanna Sternberg
label: Fat Possum
lede: They didn't write a song until their early twenties, then cut twelve of them in six days after a pandemic on the 40th floor, and Pitchfork put the result at No. 34 for 2023.

eras.title: Manhattan Plaza kid
eras.text: Joanna Sternberg grows up in a Manhattan apartment tower full of working artists, studies double bass, and writes no songs at all until their early twenties.

years.src: Wikipedia: Joanna Sternberg · The Line of Best Fit · Rough Trade
years.h: Born in New York City, raised among artists
years.p: Their father is a guitarist, songwriter and visual artist; their mother is a theatre actress. Piano lessons start at five.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Sternberg taught themself guitar and electric bass at eleven, went to LaGuardia High School, where they started double bass, and won a scholarship to the Mannes School of Music before finishing at the New School's jazz program.

The Line of Best Fit and Rough Trade both place the family in Manhattan Plaza, a 40-story subsidized building long home to working performers, where Sternberg later wrote the songs for I've Got Me.

years.src: Wikipedia: Joanna Sternberg · Get In Her Ears · The Vinyl Factory
years.h: A bassist who didn't write songs starts writing songs
years.p: Wikipedia says Sternberg began writing at 23 and performing at 24, after years of classical and jazz double bass. They also draw comics, and the drawings end up on their record sleeves.
years.xp:
Get In Her Ears reports Sternberg played bass in jazz bands and learned to sing at twenty-one. They became a regular at small New York rooms such as Union Pool and Sunny's Bar.

In the Vinyl Factory interview they call the drawing and the music "one in the same effort."

eras.title: Team Love, then Fat Possum
eras.text: A debut on Conor Oberst's label, a road education as his opener, and a word-of-mouth record that a bigger label picks up.

years.p: Wikipedia dates Sternberg's first North American tour, as Oberst's opener, to July 2018. Rough Trade places an Oberst tour in 2019 and 2020.
years.xp: Sources disagree on the year, so the date here is the one Wikipedia gives. Every account agrees on the pairing: an Oberst audience, a stage with one person and a guitar.

years.src: Wikipedia: Then I Try Some More · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Then I Try Some More, out on Team Love
years.p: Nine songs in 25:51, produced by Sternberg and Joe Rogers. Pitchfork gave it 7.5, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone's Jonathan Bernstein called it a "gorgeous bedroom lo-fi rendering of mid-century blues, jazz, and pop" and set it beside Daniel Johnston and Randy Newman. By 2023 Rolling Stone was calling it a word-of-mouth cult favorite.

Pitchfork's Emma Madden wrote that it deals with suicidal ideation, hopelessness and self-hatred, and could be "life-savingly relatable." Phoebe Bridgers has described Sternberg as an "emo Randy Newman," according to The Line of Best Fit.

years.src: Wikipedia: Then I Try Some More · Wikipedia: Joanna Sternberg · Rough Trade
years.h: Then I Try Some More gets a second release on Fat Possum
years.p: Fat Possum Records reissues the debut. Rough Trade dates Sternberg's signing to 2022.
years.xp: The same year, Wikipedia says Sternberg co-wrote the songs for the musical Corsicana with the playwright Will Arbery.

eras.title: Six days at Strange Weather
eras.text: A pandemic's worth of songs written alone on the 40th floor get cut in a week with Matt Sweeney behind the glass.

years.cap: Joanna Sternberg at Codfish Hollow Barnstormers, Maquoketa, IA 7/27/19 · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: I've Got Me · Clash · DIY Magazine
years.h: Six days at Strange Weather with Matt Sweeney
years.p: Sweeney produces and Daniel Schlett engineers. Sternberg plays every instrument.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says I've Got Me was recorded in six days at Strange Weather in Brooklyn. Sweeney says he "pretty much stayed out of Joanna's way," per Wikipedia.

DIY Magazine says the songs were written while Sternberg was stuck in the 40th-floor apartment. Sternberg told DIY: "Writing songs there was one thing that felt safe, it really saved me."

years.p: Clash reports the minimalist title song, mostly voice and guitar, led the rollout. Sternberg says its sentiment matches Charles Bukowski's poem "Oh Yes," which they have tattooed on their right arm.
years.xp: The line "There are worse things than being alone" is, per The Line of Best Fit, where Sternberg took the idea from.

years.src: Wikipedia: I've Got Me · Stereogum · The Vinyl Factory
years.h: I've Got Me is out on Fat Possum
years.p: Twelve songs, 32:34. Wikipedia lists a Pitchfork score of 8.6 and "Best New Music"; Metacritic shows 85 from five critics.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's reception box lists Pitchfork 8.6, Paste 8.0 and The Line of Best Fit 8 out of 10. Stereogum made it album of the week, writing that honesty and specificity are the qualities every songwriter should strive for.

Sternberg drew the cover art themself; the Vinyl Factory reports the first drawing they liked was roughly the hundredth attempt.

years.p: Pitchfork named I've Got Me the 34th best album of 2023 after a review score of 8.6, per Wikipedia. The album came out of a tower apartment, a six-day session and one person playing everything.

years.h: On the road with Kurt Vile and Angel Olsen
years.p: Get In Her Ears lists 2023 tour dates opening for Kurt Vile and Angel Olsen, and a possible UK run. The record release show was at the DIY venue The Glove.
years.xp: The Glove has since closed, Get In Her Ears notes.
